alternatives: Committing derived JSONL with a union merge driver (fails on forges); committing with a custom merge driver (not consulted in bare repos); no committed files at all (loses shared team memory).
consequences: Fresh clones rebuild the graph on first MCP startup. Summaries survive via summaries.jsonl. Any future committed RepoSkein file must be authored-only and merge-safe by construction.
context: nodes.jsonl and edges.jsonl are a pure function of the working tree, rebuilt in seconds. Committing them made every branch that touches code rewrite two machine-generated files, so every open PR conflicted the moment any other merged. gitattributes merge=union could not rescue this: forges compute mergeability in a bare repo where tree-level gitattributes is never consulted, and where union does apply it keeps both sides' lines, duplicating ids.
decided_by: marcus (ratified in session, recorded by claude)
decision: Derived JSONL (nodes.jsonl, edges.jsonl) stays out of git and is rebuilt from the working tree on demand. Authored data agents write (summaries, and later decision records) is committed - nothing can regenerate it.
title: Stop committing the derived graph; commit summaries instead
